task: Build a transparent geospatial levelized-cost model to estimate the delivered cost of African green hydrogen to Europe (via ammonia shipping and reconversion) by 2030 under multiple financing and policy scenarios, identify least-cost/competitive locations, and quantify how de-risking and the interest-rate environment change cost competitiveness relative to producing green hydrogen in Europe.

method_commitments.geospatial_model: Hexagon-based spatial LCOH model computing site-specific delivered costs
method_commitments.pathway: Ammonia (NH3) synthesis → trucking → maritime shipping → cracking at Rotterdam
method_commitments.interest_rate_scenarios: Three rate environments (low, moderate rise +2pp, extreme rise +4pp) per Schmidt et al. 2019
method_commitments.competitive_locations: Identify least-cost sites and quantify competitiveness thresholds
method_commitments.european_comparison: Benchmark against European domestic green hydrogen production costs

related_work_sources: Halloran et al. (GeoH2 model, Namibia case study)
Muller et al. (GEOH2 Kenya, LCOH 1.8-3.0 EUR/kg by 2030)
Schmidt et al. (Interest rate impacts on RE, Nature Sustainability 2019)
Steffen (Cost of capital for RE projects, Energy Economics 2020)
